motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Eagle Mountain City Transportation Master Plan. City Engineer Chris Trusty presented the changes as discussed during the work session. Councilmember Wright recommended tabling the item to resolve concerns and finalize details. Councilmember Love said she sees no need for Old Airport Road to follow the proposed trajectory if the future freeway is being relocated. She would like to review and better understand the impacts of the proposed changes in alignment before approving the plan and agrees that it would be beneficial to have Old Airport Road and the future freeway lined with commercial uses, open space, or decorative features to provide buffering for residential areas. Discussion ensued regarding uncertainty with land acquisition, the potential need to abandon certain areas of the road once the freeway is completed, and possible solutions. Mr. Trusty stated that he is unable to move forward with the impact fees facility plan until the Transportation Master Plan is approved and a landowner has been waiting on the finalization of the plan to be able to sell property. He recognized the Council’s desire to get the details of the plan correct but noted master plans generally exclude the finer details of the projects. He confirmed that the Council will be reviewing and voting upon the expansion of Old Airport Road independent of this approval. It might prove beneficial to contact the property owners to evaluate the likelihood of the City being able to purchase the land necessary to change the alignment. Mayor Westmoreland explained the challenges the City faces with future transportation in this area for Old Airport Road and the future freeway. Discussion determined to table the item and to assign two Councilmembers to work with staff and the consultants on amending the plan.
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to table an ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, adopting the Eagle Mountain City Transportation Master Plan to the next meeting. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
